NM-2026-SM28.title: STUDY GUN VIOLENCE
NM-2026-SM28.aiSummary: The memorial would ask the Crime Victims Reparation Commission to convene a statewide crime prevention task force to study gun violence in New Mexico and make recommendations. The group would include people from state agencies, law enforcement, schools, health care, tribes and pueblos, gun advocates, and violence prevention groups. It would study causes of gun violence, review gun laws, look at public education on safe gun ownership and storage, and report its findings to legislative committees and the governor.

NM-2026-SB33.title: RIGHT TO TRY INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENTS ACT

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB33.aiSummary: The bill would let people with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses try a custom investigational treatment made for them based on their genetic profile. It would let a manufacturer offer the treatment at a health facility, and a patient could ask for it with written, informed consent; the manufacturer could give it for free or charge the patient for the cost. The bill would also bar state officials from blocking access, protect health care providers from discipline for making such a recommendation, and say heirs would not owe debt for the treatment if the patient dies.

NM-2026-SB289.title: PUBLIC PEACE, HEALTH, SAFETY & WELFARE
NM-2026-SB289.aiSummary: A measure tied to public peace, health, safety, and welfare was postponed indefinitely in the Senate Conservation Committee.

NM-2026-SB162.title: NONPROFIT AGREEMENTS WITH DEPT. OF DEFENSE

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee

NM-2026-SB162.policyArea: MILITARY AFFAIRS (national guard, vets), PROPERTY (conservancy districts, land grants, real estate)
NM-2026-SB162.aiSummary: Regional housing authorities in New Mexico could form nonprofit groups to make support deals with the U.S. Department of Defense and its service branches. Those groups could work on leasing, building, fixing, or managing property inside or outside New Mexico. Money from those activities would go to affordable housing goals of the housing authority that created the nonprofit.

NM-2026-SB15.title: HEALTH CARE PROVIDER COVERAGE

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Health and Public Affairs Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee

NM-2026-SB15.aiSummary: The bill would require many New Mexico health plans and insurers to cover any type of health care provider when that provider is working within their legal scope of practice. It would apply to individual and group plans, health maintenance organization contracts, and nonprofit health care plans. It would take effect for plans and contracts entered into, renewed, extended, amended, or issued on or after July 1, 2026.

NM-2026-SB149.title: PROPERTY TAX CODE DEFINITIONS

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee

NM-2026-SB149.policyArea: PROPERTY (conservancy districts, land grants, real estate), TAXATION, PROPERTY
NM-2026-SB149.aiSummary: The bill would change the property tax code definition of "residential property." It would cover manufactured homes and other structures used mainly as homes, even if they are leased or rented to lodgers for any length of time. It would not treat hotels, motels, and similar commercial buildings as residential property.

NM-2026-SB112.title: SEVERANCE TAX FUND INVESTMENT CLASSES

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB112.aiSummary: The bill would change the types of investments allowed for New Mexico’s severance tax permanent fund. It would limit some “differential rate” investments, which are special investments meant to help the state economy, and clarify that other investments are “market rate” investments. It would affect how state fund managers invest money in the fund.

NM-2026-SB103.title: UNLAWFUL INTERFERENCE WITH AIRCRAFT

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Judiciary Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB103.aiSummary: The bill would update New Mexico’s aircraft law to treat directing a laser at a flying aircraft, along with firing a gun or launching an object at it, as unlawful interference. It would make a first offense a fourth-degree felony, with stronger penalties for later offenses or if someone on the aircraft needs medical treatment. It would also define the word "laser" in the law and repeal one older section on this topic.

NM-2026-HB320.title: INDUSTRIAL CARBON REDUCTION ACT

actions.text: Sent to House Energy, Environment and Natural Resources Committee & House Appropriations & Finance Committee
not printed House Rules and Order of Business Committee

NM-2026-HB320.aiSummary: The bill would create two programs in the Economic Development Department: one for production incentives and one for investment grants for New Mexico industrial facilities that cut carbon intensity. It would also require the Economic Development Department and the Department of Environment to set rules, set industry benchmarks, and use a new fund for these payments. The bill says incentives could pay $85 per ton of carbon dioxide reduced below the benchmark, and grants could cover 10% of qualified costs up to $5 million.

NM-2026-HB195.title: COLLECTION OF MEDICAL MALPRACTICE JUDGEMENTS

actions.text: DO PASS, as amended, committee report adopted
DO NOT PASS, replaced with committee substitute
Sent to House Health & Human Services Committee & House Judiciary Committee
not printed House Rules and Order of Business Committee

NM-2026-HB195.aiSummary: The bill would stop people from collecting a medical malpractice court order to pay from an independent provider’s personal income or personal property in most cases. It would cover certain licensed health workers, like doctors, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants, if a court finds they kept required malpractice coverage or had at least $1 million in insurance per claim. It would apply to medical malpractice claims brought after the bill’s effective date.

NM-2026-HB190.title: HOMELESSNESS SERVICES FOR LGBTQ+

actions.text: Sent to House Health & Human Services Committee & House Appropriations & Finance Committee

NM-2026-HB190.policyArea: PROPERTY (conservancy districts, land grants, real estate), PUBLIC ASSISTANCE (programs)
NM-2026-HB190.aiSummary: The bill would set aside $1 million from the general fund for the Workforce Solutions Department to spend in fiscal year 2027. The money would support lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer people who are experiencing homelessness with eviction prevention and housing help. Any money left over at the end of fiscal year 2027 would go back to the general fund.
